title: Canonical derived quotients as explicit coefficient complexes with compatible finite-free retracts
statement: Let X be a scheme, d an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], P a bounded finite-projective A-complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and L_n specified left adjoints to exact derived quotient restriction. There exist a complex tower T over the completed coefficient ring and a cone c such that: in every degree their diagram and cone are compatible split retracts of finite powers of the actual coefficient diagram and its completed-unit cone [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-coefficient-limit]; T localized levelwise is isomorphic to the completed constant realization of the canonical algebraic quotient diagram of P [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-quotient-diagram]; and Q(c.pt) is isomorphic to completed derived constant realization of P. The assertion makes no inverse-limit or Roos claim, and assumes no completeness of A or geometric local-model data.

source.place: Tag 09C6, the finite-projective quotient and cone comparison preceding the inverse-limit calculation; Modules on Sites, Tags 093J--093M; More on Algebra, Tag 09AW.

proof.text: Construct ordinary completed constant realization H and the tower obtained by tensoring H(P) termwise with the actual coefficient diagram. Its cone has point H(P), and the actual coefficient projections after the inverse right unitor. Tensor naturality proves commutation with every differential; mapping the coefficient cone and extending along the inverse right unitor proves all transition equations. These are explicit definitions in FinitePerfectAdicFreeTensorCone.

For each term P^j use Mathlib Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective to obtain maps g:P^j→A^r and f:A^r→P^j with g followed by f equal to the identity. Map these under H and under its tensor diagram functor. The finite-free normalization provides e and e0 identifying the free diagram and cone with the finite powers of the coefficient diagram and unit. Define the diagram inclusion by O(H(g)) followed by e, and its projection by e inverse followed by O(H(f)); do the same at the cone point with e0. Functoriality and cancellation of the isomorphisms prove both splittings. Tensor-projection naturality and the free cone equation give the inclusion square; cancel e0 and e to obtain its inverse equation, then compose with f to get the projection square. Thus every degree has the required compatible retract.

Projective modules are flat. Apply the bounded-flat tensor comparison to P and the given bounds. Its two isomorphisms compare the explicitly constructed diagram and point with the canonical derived quotient diagram and completed derived realization. Pair them with the degreewise compatible retracts. The original statement and all chosen adjunctions are unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem finitePerfectAdicCanonical_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (L : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))))
    (adj : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⊣ DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction d.ideal n)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{t} A) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Finite A (P.X i)) :
    ∃ (T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules X d) ℤ) (c : Cone T),
      (∀ j : ℤ, Nonempty (FinitePerfectAdicCoefficientRetract X d
        (T ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval (CompletedAdicModules X d) (.up ℤ) j)
        ((HomologicalComplex.eval (CompletedAdicModules X d) (.up ℤ) j).mapCone c))) ∧
      Nonempty (T ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
        finitePerfectAdicQuotientDiagram d.ideal L adj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ⋙
          finitePerfectAdicDerivedConstant X A ⋙
            completedAdicDerivedChange X (completedAdicScalar X d)) ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj c.pt ≅
        (completedAdicDerivedChange X (completedAdicScalar X d)).obj
          ((finitePerfectAdicDerivedConstant X A).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)))
